In a neutral atom, the number of electrons always equals the number of protons, not neutrons. The number of neutrons can vary, which is why isotopes of the same element exist.

Cesium (Cs) has the lowest electronegativity and Fluorine (F) has the highest electronegativity, creating the largest electronegativity difference and highest ionic character.
In boron trifluoride (BF₃), the central boron atom shares 3 pairs of electrons, giving it a total of only 6 valence electrons around it.

Valence electrons in metals are delocalized and free to move throughout the crystal lattice, easily carrying electrical current and heat energy.
Because oxygen is highly electronegative and small, hydrogen atoms bonded to oxygen in H₂O form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds, requiring more thermal energy to separate.
Carbon dioxide is linear. The polar C=O bond dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel each other out completely, resulting in zero net dipole moment.
Oxygen has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs. The repulsion between lone pairs forces the O-H bonds into a bent or V-shaped geometry.

Nitrogen has atomic number 7, so a neutral atom has 7 electrons. Filling sub-shells in order of increasing energy gives 1s² 2s² 2p³. The s sub-shells hold 4 electrons in total (2 in 1s and 2 in 2s), and the p sub-shell (2p) holds 3 electrons.
Relative atomic mass takes into account both the mass and the natural abundance percentage of each isotope (like Cl-35 and Cl-37), making it a weighted average rather than a simple average.
A mass spectrometer separates ions based on their mass-to-charge ratio to determine the relative isotopic masses and abundances, allowing the calculation of the relative atomic mass of an element.

Isotopes are atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but a different number of neutrons, and so different mass numbers.

Nuclear attraction depends on the distance from the nucleus and on the nuclear charge. A 1s electron is closest to the nucleus, and among the 1s options potassium has the most protons (19), so its 1s electrons feel the strongest pull.
